name: Nora Keane
greet: Evening. The usual, when you're ready.
Is the fire in? Grand. A pint of stout, please.
praise: Now that's a pint worth waiting for.
You've the knack of it, I'll give you that.
complain: Hm. Your predecessor rushed his pints too.
That head's all over the place, love.
chat: I taught half this town to read. The other half taught themselves to sing.
This pub had a piano once. Someone should bring one back.
Rain again. Good for the gardens, bad for the hair.

name: Declan Moran
greet: Long day. Something cold, please.
Pint please, before I fall over.
praise: Lovely job. Exactly what I needed.
complain: Bit of a wait there, chief.
chat: Did three ceilings today. My shoulders are in bits.
You should get those walls done. I'd give you a price.
The match is on Saturday. Big one.

name: Aoife Brennan
greet: Off shift at last. Something cold, please.
Hiya! The usual for me.
complain: That took a while, didn't it?
chat: Twelve hours on my feet. This stool is heaven.
My granny drank in here in the sixties. Says it was mad back then.
You should do a quiz night. I'd come.

name: Packie Walsh
greet: Well. Pint of the black stuff.
Is the board up yet? No? Pint so.
praise: That's a proper job. Proper job.
complain: In my day you'd be fired for that.
Give it a minute next time, son.
chat: I once hit three treble twenties at a wedding. Nobody believes me.
Get a dartboard in and I'll be here every night.
Your stout tap's leaning a bit, you know.

name: Siobhán Gallagher
greet: Evening! Anything on tap I'd like?
One for the road, please.
complain: That's a bit sad looking, isn't it?
chat: I know everyone's business in this town. Professionally.
Somebody's ordering a lot of fiddle strings lately.
There's a storm due Friday, mark my words.

name: Tomás Hegarty
greet: Howya. Pint, please. My fingers need warming.
Same as always.
complain: That pint's a bit out of tune.
chat: If you ever clear out that corner, I'd bring a few musicians.
Played a session in Kilbrack last week. Tiny room, huge sound.
A good bodhrán player is worth their weight in gold.

name: Margaret Doyle
greet: Good evening. What do you have that's warming?
My usual, if you'd be so kind.
chat: Did you know the oldest pub in the country is over a thousand years old?
Capital of Mongolia? Ulaanbaatar. Always comes up.
I'm looking for a new quiz. The last one fell apart.

name: Liam Fitzgerald
greet: Pint please, the kids ran me ragged.
Quick one before training.
chat: We lost nine-nil. They're getting better.
You should put a telly up for the matches.
The under-12s want to do a fundraiser here.

name: Ciara Nolan
greet: Hi! Something without alcohol, please.
Can I get my usual?
chat: I play the tin whistle. Badly, but loudly.
Your jukebox should have more reels.
I'm writing an essay on session etiquette. Don't ask.

name: Eamon Kinsella
greet: Pint of stout. Don't rush it.
Evening. A stout, when it's ready.
praise: That'd put hair on your chest.
complain: That's a poor head on it.
chat: The cows don't care if it's raining. Lucky them.
Turf's good this year. I'll drop you a load for the fire.
Fifty years I've been coming in here.

name: Fionnuala Byrne
greet: Something red and hoppy, if you have it.
Evening! What's good tonight?
complain: Bit of a wait, wasn't it?
chat: I could paint you a new sign, you know.
The light in here at five o'clock is magic.
Those old photos are lovely. Who took them?
